text: 2026-10-14 23:58 to 2026-10-15 00:00 (ignition on, engine off, grey A6 cable fitted, adapter switch HS): a raw passive-listen test run directly on COM3, outside CUORE's safeguards, opened the adapter in receive-only mode on CAN-CH at 500k (correct) and ALSO at 250k and 125k (wrong speed, 3 windows of ~2 s, adapter reported CAN ERROR). Owner heard a chime and saw the AIRBAG lamp during the test. Expect a lost-communication / bus-off history code in ORC, IPC or BCM stamped in this window; it is a tool-caused artefact, NOT a vehicle fault, and must not be cleared or counted as evidence for any repair. Lesson applied in code: passive listen now uses STMA with auto-format off, and only ever at a bus's confirmed bitrate; the old route note 'if silent try STP 36 then STPBR 125000' on CAN-CH is withdrawn.

text: 2026-10-15 00:30-01:10 local, CUORE guided scan SCAN_2610141901. Blue A5 cable, CAN-IHS at 125k: passive listen on the 29-bit route heard 17 frames/2 s, all keep-alive ids 1E340000/03/0A/24/30/33/34/45/67; the 11-bit route heard 317 frames/2 s over 54 ids (3E2, 3E4, 3E6, 3E8, 2F0, 3DC, 3DE, 3E0 ...). The bus is alive. Read-only discovery (22 F190, 1.5 s wait each) to 29-bit targets 45,30,24,03,0A,33,34,67,00,68,6F,01,02 got no reply; one functional TesterPresent (3E 00 on 18DB33F1) got NO DATA. No body module has a confirmed address, so the guided segment reached no module. Grey A6 cable, CAN-CH at 500k: alive (438 frames/2 s, 33 ids). The ABS answered 22 F190 at 29-bit 0x2A once (00:08, VIN + identity) and never again, including after an ignition cycle and an adapter warm start. A timing bug (python-side wait 0.25-0.5 s shorter than the adapter's 1.02 s reply wait after ATSTFF) made the 253-address 29-bit sweep and the 239-address 11-bit sweep unreliable as negative results; fixed in code tonight. Meaning: on both bypass-cable buses listening works and transmitting gets nothing back (ABS once excepted), while MultiEcuScan reads EPS/HALF through the same grey cable. Suspect the request/receive path (adapter filters after STCFCPC/STP, flow control, ATCAF framing, 11-bit vs 29-bit diagnostics) rather than the modules. Neutral for the EVAP hypothesis. Next tests (read-only, engine running, through CUORE): lone CR then ATI; repeat 22F190 to ABS 0x2A with ATST 19 + ATAT0; ATCRA off + explicit STFAP 18DAF12A pass filter; 22F190 with ATFCSM0; raw ISO-TP first frame with ATCAF0; passive MES-learn capture of a MultiEcuScan session on CAN-CH to read the ids MES uses for EPS/HALF.

text: 2026-10-23 outside research (subagents, web + local docs; NOT CUORE readings). Newest radio software for a 2018 NA Stelvio: MV-090.000.061 per TSB 08-065-20 (2020-06-24, covers 2017-19 Giulia and 2018-19 Stelvio built 2017-10-30..2019-07-12; text read: "MV 090.000.061, ETM has the latest available software"). TSB ladder: 002.009.059 or lower (early 2.0 radio; "this software will not download to the radio") -> 072.001.002 -> 081.000.004 -> 085.000.046 -> 090.000.061; after the radio, BCM/AMP/ABS/IPC/PAM/blind-spot may need updating; phones re-paired. MV-119.001.009 exists in TSB 08-064-20 but for 2020 MY builds only; whether a 2018 unit can take it is not stated. Source files are dealer-only (DealerCONNECT > UCONNECT Command Center > Dealer software downloads, security access, wiTECH for diagnosis); blank NTFS USB 16 GB (TSB) per update; engine running; no official owner download found. NHTSA PDFs: static.nhtsa.gov/odi/tsbs/2020/MC-10177540-9999.pdf (08-065-20), /2020/MC-10223593-9999.pdf (08-064-20). Unresolved CONFLICT for this car (MV-002.009.043): the TSB says <=.059 cannot take its download, but a German forum post (alfa-romeo-portal.com thread 3597 p4, 2020-05-06) lists MV002.009.043/.053/.055/.059 as levels where only the ETM needs updating; owners there self-installed from USB (~17 min) and one went 002.009.055 -> 002.010.043 (Stelvio 2017, 2022) and a Giulia 002.009.061 -> 002.010.041. Likely realistic target is the next step in the 002 family (002.010.0xx), UNVERIFIED for North America; one source says firmware series cannot be swapped. MV vs TV: no source defines them; no TV value and no meaning for 971.7832 found anywhere. No owner cost/warranty figures found. Most US forums (alfaowner, stelvioforum, giuliaforums) paywalled, unread. Unofficial copies of 090.000.061 circulate but integrity is unverified: not downloaded, not recommended. Nothing downloaded for the radio.

text: 2026-10-24 PLAN (research, nothing bought or installed): CarPlay/Android Auto via an interface box that keeps the factory 8.8-in screen, radio, knob and steering keys. Full plan: docs/research/STELVIO_INTERFACE_BOX_DEPLOYMENT_PLAN.md (10 sections: scope, pre-install checks, box comparison with vendor questions, parts, install outline, pass/fail test plan, rollback, risks, sequencing, open questions). No product recommended; boxes compared: APPplay (navinc CP-ALF-G1PV), Abt ZZ-2 ($850), Ampire RL4-C3D (video only, 4 CVBS inputs, 8 mA standby) and the route-B boxes in INFOTAINMENT_CAMERA_UPGRADE_OPTIONS.md. Why this route: OpenAuto Pro (Raspberry Pi) was ruled out 2026-10-24: BlueWave Studio shut down, software broken by Android Auto protocol changes (community repo, archived Feb 2026), and the only Stelvio video inserter found takes composite (~480i) with no knob control. Key risk: every box found reads CAN through the radio Quadlock, and on this car the radio is on CAN-C; none is known to be CAN-passive. Test gate: read-only CUORE baseline scan before work and post-install scan after; any new CAN-C U-code = fail, record, do not clear; standby current vs vendor figure; 3-day battery rest-voltage check. Sequence: EVAP proof (job 76d3454bce75) -> dealer visit 2026-10-28 -> radio update to MV-002.010.041 per TSB 08-029-20 if build date <= 2018-01-11 -> map v1176 -> interface box. Open: 1) build date (door-jamb MDH); 2) factory AUX jack on this NA car (Abt and APPplay require it); 3) each box's minimum radio firmware and CAN-C behaviour, in writing; 4) standby current figures; 5) Canadian availability, returns, dealer attitude to a fitted box.
